**Governing Policy Rule**: Aggregate liability must be mutual and capped at no less than twelve (12) months of gross fees paid or payable. Consequential, indirect, and special damages waivers must be strictly mutual. Data privacy/security breaches, confidentiality breaches, and third-party IP indemnification obligations must be carved out from the general cap or subject to a minimum 2x–3x (24–36 months fees) Super-Cap.

**Governing Policy Rule**: All custom deliverables, bespoke configurations, integrations, and work product paid for by Customer shall be owned exclusively by Customer as "Work Made for Hire" (with a present assignment of all intellectual property rights). top_risks_requiring_attention: Clause 8 (Data Privacy, Security Incident Notification and AI Training) — Score 96/100 [Critical]: Violates POL-SEC-2026-v3.1 §2.3: Security incident notification window exceeds the strict 24-hour (or 48-hour outer regulatory) playbook mandate. Express violation of Company AI Governance Policy prohibiting Vendor from training or fine-tuning AI/ML models on Customer Data. Delays breach reporting up to 10 business days, jeopardizing GDPR/CCPA/CERT-In 72-hour regulatory reporting timelines. Missing required protection: Explicit prohibition against using Customer Data, prompts, or outputs to train shared or third-party AI/ML models.

Clause 6 (Limitation of Liability and Consequential Damages) — Score 95/100 [Critical]: Violates POL-LEGAL-2026-v4.2 §4.1: Vendor liability cap is severely below the mandatory 12-month fees floor (2x/24-month super-cap for data/IP). One-sided consequential damages waiver or exclusion of super-cap carve-outs (data breach, confidentiality, IP indemnity). Caps Vendor aggregate liability at 1–3 months of fees while exposing Customer to disproportionate loss. Missing required protection: Mutual consequential damages waiver and mandatory super-cap carve-outs for IP infringement, confidentiality, and data security breaches.

Clause 4 (Intellectual Property and Work Product Ownership) — Score 88/100 [Critical]: Violates POL-LEGAL-2026-v4.2 §3.2: Assigns ownership of paid custom deliverables and derivative works to Vendor instead of Customer ('Work Made for Hire' violation). Customer pays for custom development but only receives a revocable, non-transferable license. Missing required protection: Full ownership assignment ('Work Made for Hire') of custom deliverables and Customer-specific configurations to Customer.

Clause 5 (Indemnification Obligations) — Score 78/100 [High]: Violates POL-LEGAL-2026-v4.2 §5.1: One-way indemnification clause requiring Customer to indemnify Vendor while omitting Vendor IP infringement and data breach indemnity. Shifts all third-party litigation defense costs onto Customer without reciprocal Vendor protection. Missing required protection: Uncapped Vendor indemnification for third-party IP infringement, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and data breaches.
